newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures settle down as rise fizzles.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures settle down as rise fizzles.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Monday when a late sell-off erased the complex's gains prompted by shortcovering, a rally in natural gas futures and higher spot cash prices in the western U.S.
"We were strong all day. Then, someone came in and sold a bunch," said a Houston trader.

February California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down 18 cents at $13.73 a megawatt hour (MWh) after reaching as high as $14.35. Today's lower settlement broke an upward channel on the daily chart. which began forming last week.
March COB finished down 22 cents at $11.43, near its session low of $11.40. Other active COB months ended nine to 15 cents lower.
February Palo Verde (PV) settled down 78 cents at $15.82 after climbing to an intraday high of $16.70.
March PV finished down 53 cents at $13.60. April PV ended down 20 cents at $12.50.
Both February power contracts expire Tuesday.

Day-ahead power prices were boosted by the absence of Bonneville Power Administration. Firm, peak COB electricity for Tuesday rose to $15.50-$16.50, up 50 cents to $1.50 from Friday, while those at PV held steady at $16.00-$17.00.
Western gas prices rose, albeit in smaller increments, with the Gulf Coast market. "They did not move in lock step with the Gulf. The basis widened," said one gas marketer.

February gas deliveries at the San Juan Hub in New Mexico were assessed at $2.48-$2.53 per million British thermal unit, up slightly from Friday's $2.45-$2.50. February natgas at the Sumas point near the U.S./Canadian border rose to $2.40-$2.45.

Separately, maintenance on southbound transmissions on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie reduced power flow section to 2,000 megawatts (MW) today. The capacity of the line section is rated at 3,200 MW.
Also, an 805 MW power turbine at the Grand Coulee hydroelectric dam in Washington state began operating over the weekend after being shut last Tuesday for repairs.
Outage of 500 kilvolt transmission line, which runs from Snohomish County, Wash. to the Canadian border, was extended to later this week after ice-storm damage over a week ago.
NYMEX estimated 235 COB and 128 PV contracts were sold.
